title: Attiéké with grilled fish (Ivorian cassava couscous with tomato-onion relish)

ingredients.name: attiéké (ready-made cassava couscous, frozen or dried; couscous is a poor but workable substitute)
whole tilapia or sea bream, gutted and scaled

steps: Score the fish a few times on each side, then rub with the garlic, salt and 2 tablespoons of the oil and leave for 30 minutes.
Prepare a hot grill or grill pan, or heat the oven grill to high.
Grill the fish for 6 to 8 minutes per side, until the skin is lightly charred and the flesh is opaque and flakes at the thickest part.
Mix the tomatoes, onion, chilli, lime juice and remaining oil in a bowl and season with salt to make the relish.

If the attiéké is frozen, thaw it, then steam it in a covered colander over simmering water or in the microwave for about 5 minutes until hot and fluffy; dried attiéké is rehydrated with a little hot water first.
Fluff with a fork and mound onto plates.
Serve the grilled fish alongside the attiéké with the fresh relish spooned over the top.

title: Gnamakoudji (Ivorian ginger and pineapple drink)

ingredients.name: fresh ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
ice and fresh mint to serve

steps: Blend the ginger with the cold water until it forms a coarse, pulpy liquid.
Pour the mixture through a fine sieve lined with cheesecloth, pressing hard to extract all the juice, then discard the pulp.
Leave the ginger juice to rest for 10 minutes so the fine starch settles at the bottom, then pour off the clear liquid, leaving the sediment behind.
Stir in the pineapple juice, sugar, lemon juice and vanilla until the sugar dissolves.
Taste and adjust the sweetness or ginger kick with a little more sugar or water.
Chill thoroughly for at least 2 hours.
Serve over ice with a sprig of mint.

title: Kedjenou (Ivorian slow-cooked chicken and vegetable stew)

ingredients.name: scotch bonnet or other hot chilli, left whole

steps: Place the chicken in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid.
Add the onions, tomatoes, aubergines, garlic, ginger, whole chilli, oil and salt, and mix well with your hands.
Cover the pot with the lid, using a sheet of foil underneath to seal it if the lid is loose, so no steam escapes.
Cook over low heat for 1 hour and 15 minutes, without adding water, because the vegetables release the liquid the chicken cooks in.
Every 15 minutes, hold the lid on firmly and shake the pot back and forth to stop the food catching on the bottom.
Open the lid, check that the chicken is falling off the bone and the sauce is thick, and cook uncovered for a few minutes if it is too thin.
Remove the chilli, taste and serve with attiéké, rice or boiled yam.
